target_pattern: Use gustar with indirect object pronouns and correct agreement (gusta/gustan), including infinitive use and optional clarifiers (a Juan, a María).

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Translating I like X as Yo gusto X.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: In Spanish, the thing liked is the subject; me/te/le/nos/les marks who receives that liking.
target_pattern_formula: me/te/le/nos/les + gusta + singular noun or infinitive
Optional clarifier: A Juan le gusta...
natural_examples: A María le gustan las flores.

controlled_recombination.instructions: Write each in Spanish using gustar correctly. No answer key until the end.
prompts_en: Do Ana and Juan like music?

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Me gusta el café. -> change noun to plural (los cafés).
Base: ¿Te gusta bailar? -> change infinitive to correr.
Base: Le gustan las flores a María. -> make it singular noun (la flor).
Base: Nos gusta viajar. -> make it negative.
Base: ¿Les gusta el teatro? -> change to plural subject thing (los teatros).
Base: A Juan le gusta leer. -> turn into question.
Base: Me gustan las películas. -> change to singular (la película).
Base: ¿Te gusta el invierno? -> answer no in full sentence.
Base: A ellos les gustan los animales. -> change to feminine plural noun (las plantas).
Base: Le gusta el mar a Laura. -> change to nosotros and la playa.
Base: Nos gustan las verduras. -> change to infinitive pattern (comer verduras).
Base: ¿Le gusta cantar a María? -> change verb to bailar.
Base: Me gusta escribir. -> add another infinitive in same sentence.
Base: ¿Te gustan las flores? -> rewrite with clarifier for Juan.
Base: Les gusta la música. -> rewrite with explicit subject A mis amigos.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the most natural option and write in Spanish.
prompts: I like coffee. (me gusta vs yo gusto)
I like books. (me gustan los libros vs me gusta los libros)
I like to dance. (me gusta bailar vs me gustan bailar)
Do you like chocolate? (¿te gusta el chocolate? vs ¿te gustan el chocolate?)
We like vegetables. (nos gustan las verduras vs nos gusta las verduras)
Juan likes music. (a Juan le gusta la música vs Juan gusta la música)
They like to travel. (les gusta viajar vs les gustan viajar)
Do Ana and Juan like movies? (¿a Ana y a Juan les gustan las películas? vs ¿a Ana y a Juan le gustan...?)
I do not like that. (no me gusta eso vs no gusto eso)
Do you like me? (¿te gusto? vs ¿te gusta yo?)

You like learning Spanish every day.
Your partner or friend likes your new plan.

common_errors.mistake: Using yo gusto for I like

common_errors.why_it_happens: Infinitives are treated as plural actions.

common_errors.mistake: Wrong recipient pronoun le vs les
common_errors.correct_spanish: A Juan le gusta... / A Juan y Ana les gusta...

common_errors.mistake: Dropping article with noun after gustar

common_errors.correct_spanish: Pronoun-only form is natural when context is clear.

common_errors.mistake: Using subject pronouns as gustar subjects
common_errors.why_it_happens: I/you are assumed to be subject as in English.

common_errors.mistake: Literal English word order in questions
Confusing Te gusto with Te gusta yo
